φῠλᾰκ-τήριον , τό,
A.guarded post, fort, castle,
Hdt. 5.52 : esp. an outpost communicating with fortifications,
Th. 4.31 , 33 , 110 , X. Cyr. 7.5.12 : pl., guardrooms,
Arist. Pol. 1331a20 .
2. safeguard, security,
Pl. Lg. 917b : preservative,
D. 6.24 ; amulet,
Dsc. 5.154 , Plu. 2.378b , etc.; among the Jews φυλακτήρια were small rolls of parchment with texts from the Law written on them, bound to the forehead by persons praying,
Ev.Matt. 23.5 ; φ. χρυσᾶ, symbols denoting the kingdoms of Upper and Lower Egypt, OGI 90.45 (Rosetta, ii B. C.); amulet,
PMag.Lond. 121.298 (pl.); metaph., “τὸ ὄνομά σου ἔχω ἓν φ. ἐν καρδίᾳ”
PMag.Leid.W. 18.2
.
3. perh. guard or chain, PLond.ined. 2199 .
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
